what_it_does: It produces variants of the customer's advertisement in different aspect ratios as requested by the customer, with custom font and logo and text content, as input by the customer in the API call.
how_it_works: Three stages: (1) De-brand — an instruction-tuned edit model erases all baked-in text and logos from the hero; a diff-based composite keeps the  customer's original pixels everywhere except the erased patches. (2)  Re-aspect — each format is produced by true masked outpainting (only the new canvas area is synthesized, color-matched to the original), so the hero is never regenerated. (3) Re-brand — a deterministic compositing stage applies logo, brand colors, Google Fonts typography and tone-driven layouts with automatic legibility and per-format safe zones. Hero preservation is structural, not prompted; identical payloads return identical pixels; the whole stack is Apache-licensed open weights.
flexibility: hero_image (URL — direct file link to PNG/JPG/WebP/SVG; may be a finished ad, baked-in text/logos are removed automatically) · brand_kit_logo (URL — PNG/JPG/SVG, transparency respected, overlaid as designed) · brand_kit_primary_color1 / brand_kit_primary_color2  (#RRGGBB) · brand_kit_font (Google Font name, e.g. "Inter", or direct .ttf/.otf URL) · brand_kit_tone (playful | premium | technical | minimal — selects the layout grammar) · audience_cut1_label/headline/subhead …  audience_cut4_label/headline/subhead (free text; headline and subhead  are rendered, label is metadata) · format1 … format4 (1:1 → 1080×1080, 4:5 → 1080×1350, 9:16 → 1080×1920, 16:9 → 1920×1080; arbitrary "W:H" ratios also accepted). All keys must be present in the call; pass "" (or the sentinel "none" in form UIs) for unused cut/format slots — those paths are skipped. Output: one PNG per provided cut × format pair, grouped per format, file counter = cut order (deterministic naming).
judges_notes: It was a bit unclear on what exactly was wished for in terms of safe zones, logo placements and such, so I built a logic that finds the optimal contrast on the upper part of the image. I determined the upper part placement so that it should be below any UI elements that tiktok or such channels would place there. It would be trivial to change this, in case "safe zones" was supposed to mean something else.

what_it_does: The workflow makes a variant of an ad design and transforms it into a brand-supported version with the aid of reference images and prompt instructions. It lets you take any layout and smartly resize it for different aspect ratios, while giving you the freedom to swap in logos, add secondary images, and tweak design details so that the final product stays perfectly on-brand.
how_it_works:
The workflow is powered by a custom ComfyUI node created for Nanobanana to facilitate the layout transition. This custom node gathers the original design, the target aspect ratio, and all of the brand assets, and coordinates them with a multimodal AI model. 
A dynamic prompt pipeline feeds these inputs into the model, instructing it on how to intelligently rearrange the composition, preserve the core design styles, and fit everything naturally into the new layout without losing the original visual hierarchy.
flexibility:
supported aspect ratios: 1:1, 4:5, 5:4, 3:2, 4:3, 16:9, 21:9, 2:3, 3:4, 9:16
example prompt 1:
'change 'A wonderful Night with ' to '2 For $7'
change 'The Kirby's Show' to 'We Have The Meats'
respect the color scheme of the logo. Place the logo in a prominent place
remove the remaining bottom texts
feature the models in the provided image in an appealing way as the background.'

example prompt 2:
'change 'Stay Loud' to 'Getting Money!'
color schemes should be #1F143D, #FFFFFF, #6C00FF, #AF5BFF
at the bottom-left corner, put a small corebridge logo'
judges_notes: It might not always respect provided fonts.
